chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated.' He said, 'The intoxication of sleep.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'intoxicated' mean in the Quranic verse about prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a nuanced exegesis of Surah An-Nisa 4:43, interpreting 'intoxication' not merely as alcohol-induced stupor but as 'sukr al-nawm' (the intoxication of deep sleep). This interpretation underscores the necessity of conscious awareness (hudur al-qalb) for valid prayer, linking the physical state of wakefulness to the spiritual requirement of presence, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the conditions of Salah.
